sequences.title: Free/Busy Request and Reply Component Semantics

intro.quote: A "VFREEBUSY" calendar component is a grouping of component properties that represents either a request for free or busy time information, a reply to a request for free or busy time information, or a published set of busy time information.

steps.explain: The request identifies the calendar user whose free or busy time is being requested, while the ORGANIZER property identifies the requester.

cite.quote: When used to request free/busy time information, the "ATTENDEE" property specifies the calendar users whose free/busy time is being requested; the "ORGANIZER" property specifies the calendar user who is requesting the free/busy time;

steps.segment: reply to a request for free/busy time
steps.explain: The attendee replies with any available free or busy time information, while the organizer remains identified as the original requester.

cite.quote: When used to reply to a request for free/busy time, the "ATTENDEE" property specifies the calendar user responding to the free/busy time request; the "ORGANIZER" property specifies the calendar user that originally requested the free/busy time; the "FREEBUSY" property specifies the free/busy time information (if it exists);

fields.name: name
fields.explain: The property identifier at the start of the content line.

fields.name: param
fields.explain: Optional semicolon-prefixed parameter groups, each giving a parameter name and value.

fields.name: value
fields.explain: The property-specific value following the colon.

cite.quote: The property value component of a content line has a format that is property specific.  Refer to the section describing each property for a definition of this format.

fields.name: CRLF
fields.explain: The carriage-return and line-feed pair that terminates each content line.

cite.quote: Content lines are delimited by a line break, which is a CRLF sequence (CR character followed by LF character).

fields.name: BEGIN:VCALENDAR
fields.explain: The opening delimiter of the iCalendar object.

cite.quote: They SHOULD be specified after the "BEGIN:VCALENDAR" delimiter string and prior to any calendar component.

fields.name: calendar properties
fields.explain: Object-wide properties placed after the opening delimiter and before any calendar component.

cite.quote: The Calendar Properties are attributes that apply to the iCalendar object, as a whole.  These properties do not appear within a calendar component.  They SHOULD be specified after the "BEGIN:VCALENDAR" delimiter string and prior to any calendar component.

fields.name: calendar components
fields.explain: Collections of properties expressing a calendar semantic, such as an event, to-do, journal entry, time zone, free/busy information, or alarm.

cite.quote: The calendar components are collections of properties that express a particular calendar semantic.  For example, the calendar component can specify an event, a to-do, a journal entry, time zone information, free/busy time information, or an alarm.

fields.name: END:VCALENDAR
fields.explain: The closing delimiter of the iCalendar object.

intro.quote: A "VEVENT" calendar component is a grouping of component properties, possibly including "VALARM" calendar components, that represents a scheduled amount of time on a calendar.

fields.name: BEGIN:VEVENT
fields.explain: The opening delimiter of the event component.

fields.name: component properties
fields.explain: The properties that describe the scheduled event.

cite.quote: A "VEVENT" calendar component is a grouping of component properties, possibly including "VALARM" calendar components, that represents a scheduled amount of time on a calendar.

fields.name: VALARM
fields.explain: An optional nested component that defines an alarm for the event.

cite.quote: A "VEVENT" calendar component is a grouping of component properties, possibly including "VALARM" calendar components, that represents a scheduled amount of time on a calendar.

fields.name: END:VEVENT
fields.explain: The closing delimiter of the event component.
